messages:
jess: FYI seeing a sudden spike of 504s in us-east-1 since ~11:00 UTC. Affected route: POST /v1/generate (streaming). Envoy returns 504 upstream connect timeout. Customers reporting stalled streams. trace sample: 7a3f2b9c
jess: rate ~2.5% errors, p99 latency jumped from 220ms -> 18s for that route. Mostly traffic hitting r10 routing group.
lina_support: which customers? any repro? can you grab a curl that reproduces?
jess: multiple customers. quick curl that reproduces in my dev org (non-prod token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat token)" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"hello"}' -N
```
jess: behaviour: connection opens then stalls, eventually Envoy returns 504. tcpdump from edge shows SYN/handshake then long wait to upstream.
omar_sre: do we have any recent infra/config rollouts around 11:00? envoy/nginx or authsvc?
deploy-bot: deploy log: auth-service v2.3.1 rolled to us-east-1 at 10:58 UTC by @marta_eng. Config change: lowered http2_max_concurrent_streams on auth upstream (reason: mitigate head-of-line in auth pool).
marta_eng: I rolled a small http2 tweak to auth after seeing streaming overload yesterday. didn't expect this to affect connect latency. investigating.
omar_sre: can you pull envoy stats (upstream_rq_pending_overflow, upstream_cx_connect_fail) and authsvc latency p95/p99?
jess: envoy stats show upstream_cx_connect_timeout spikes on r10 pool around 11:00. authsvc p99 spiked from 80ms -> 1.2s around same time. also seeing >200 keepalive resets.
marta_eng: looking at authsvc logs, saw a burst of TLS renegotiation errors and GC pauses right after deploy. GC logs: multiple >300ms STW events.
authsvc-bot: [alert] high_gc: auth-service instance i-0a12 reported 4 GC pauses >300ms in 5m window.
omar_sre: hypothesis: lowering http2 concurrent streams reduced per-connection throughput -> many new connections -> TLS handshakes + GC -> connect latency -> Envoy timed out -> 504s. streaming requests are more sensitive because they hold connections open.
lina_support: customer-facing note draft? we need a quick explanation and ETA.
marta_eng: immediate mitigation: rolling back the http2_max_concurrent_streams change and restarting 3 authsvc pods in us-east-1. also increasing upstream conn pool size on Envoy for a quick test.
omar_sre: apply rollback and bump timeout for /v1/generate route from 15s -> 45s as temporary measure. also add more aggressive keepalive for auth upstream.
jess: rolled back and restarted at 11:18 UTC. bumped route timeout at 11:21 UTC. initial metrics: error rate dropped to 0.6% in 5m post-fix, p99 latency back to ~300ms for most traffic.
lina_support: sending this to affected customers: short note with apology, summary of cause (auth config + GC + TLS churn), mitigation, and follow-up.
marta_eng: postmortem actions: 1) revert risky http2 change until we can load-test 2) add canary that exercises streaming routes during auth changes 3) tune authGC settings and upgrade JVM to 11.0.19 to reduce STW pauses 4) add Envoy circuit-breaker alert for upstream_cx_connect_timeout > 0.5% over 5m.
omar_sre: I'll own the Envoy alert and the temporary timeout rollback. @marta_eng please own auth GC tuning.
jess: repro steps saved in internal runbook: 1) use streaming curl above 2) hit with 50 concurrent streams to r10 group 3) watch envoy stats and auth p99 4) if 504s reproduce, check http2_max_concurrent_streams and GC.
authsvc-bot: created ticket AUTH-3148: investigate GC spikes and revert http2 param.
lina_support: thanks team. customer comms sent at 11:35 UTC. will reopen if residual errors persist. :thumbsup:
